content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/19/gtavi-21-1795111175449.jpg

Enough people to fill a third of New Zealand’s population changed their console settings to play GTA 6 a day early. Dubbed the “ New Zealand trick ,” the exploit saw players change their region to appear as if they were in another country where the clock struck midnight earliest.

This happens fairly often for games with a local midnight launch, but GTA 6 saw an unprecedented number of people pretending to be Kiwis. 2 million U.S. and U.K. players took a little trip to New Zealand on November 18 on Xbox alone, according to Ampere Analysis.

1.5m Xbox users in the U.S. took advantage of the loophole, and 600,000 U.K. Xbox users jumped right in with them. The data also only shows some of the story. Playing early is as easy as changing a setting on Xbox, but PlayStation players have to create a whole new account based in the country, and import PSN currency to spend on the store.

These frustrating hoops mean the number was likely significantly lower on PS5, but it probably still wasn’t an insignificant number of people considering GTA 6 game sales are expected to lean heavily towards Sony’s platform. So, the total number of fans using the New Zealand trick will be higher.

New Zealand's official tourism board recently celebrated the launch of GTA 6 by welcoming gamers taking advantage of the trick. "One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," said the post on the New Zealand tourist board's Instagram account.
"We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you."

While technically against the terms and services of Xbox and PlayStation, the loophole seems to be an accepted grey area for Microsoft and Sony, in so much as neither has said or done anything to clamp down (we've asked for comment). In fact, Xbox has flaunted the trick as a feature for previous game releases. “Kia Ora to all the people who moved to NZ last night!” Microsoft said a Twitter post from Xbox in 2021, celebrating the launch of Forza Horizon 5.
Whether you took the trip or managed to white knuckle it through to the official launch, GTA 6 is finally here and it’s worth the wait. GTA 6 is now the highest rated game of all time . Crikey.

items.title: 即使是我们这些顽固的 PC 游戏玩家也不会被 GTA 6 中 30 fps 所困扰
items.summary: The game wears it surprisingly well, though we'll be less happy if the PC version is similarly capped.

content.v: For a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer. Yes, if you try to insult XCOM, you're going to get a slap, but we've only just started playing GTA 6 ( well, some of us ) and we're mostly over the whole 'only runs at 30 fps' thing already.

It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.

GTA 6 certainly does that. That's the impression I get from most members of the team that have played it so far. Though if Rockstar is listening, when you do get around to our precious PC version, we'd love nothing more than 4K60—maybe more.
James Bentley, Hardware Writer
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/nXJvUmhon9WghwJuvDVoHR-1920-80.png

I will no doubt appreciate frames above 100 fps when GTA 6 comes to PC. Heck, I'd even just appreciate going up to 60 fps. But in my handful of hours with the game thus far, I just have simply not been that bothered by it. Be it smart ways of masking low frames, or even just the slower, methodical control approach of the game, I'm less frustrated with my PS5 running the game at around 30 fps than I was recently playing Phantom Blade Zero at well above 40 fps on a handheld PC.

Maybe that's down to the world having a little bit of magic to it, maybe it's the engrossing tone and atmosphere, maybe it's just because it looks so darn pretty. Maybe it's because I haven't got to the game's most hectic moments yet and haven't really needed to hit a headshot with my console unable to keep up with me. I'll tell you how I'm getting on in another fifty hours. Cool, see you in three days, then?
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/GgdsawGpbSzorU9FDRha5E-1920-80.jpg
Fraser Brown, Online Editor
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/o5oYVAFnHjesaVgoJsQD9E-1920-80.png

I was dreading playing GTA 6 on my OG PS5—a dusty ornament that's been chilling out in my living room this last year doing absolutely nothing. I've got a nice gaming PC in my office (RTX 4090, Intel i9 13900K, 32 GB RAM), so it's been a long time since I've had to deal with games dipping below 80 fps. I have been spoiled.

The second I got to control Lucia, my fears seemed justified. Everything just felt sluggish. But that feeling didn't last. I played GTA 6 for around 5 hours last night (I am very tired) and I haven't thought about the frame rate once since that initial section. Whether I'm getting into shootouts with coke smugglers, speeding through the Keys at night, or bouncing around at sea, GTA 6 looks great and feels great.
I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth.
Fraser Brown

I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth. I'm sure I've encountered drops, but crucially I haven't noticed them. Sure, it's inevitably going to look better and run better on PC, but the lower performance on my PS5 quickly ceased to be an issue, and I'm not regretting playing it on console.
Phil Savage, Global Editor-in-Chief
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/4sHLcbB96zPH9vjoBAiMYC-1920-80.png

GTA 6 is the kind of game where an uncapped framerate would be nice, but it doesn't feel essential. Like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it—a game I also played at 30 fps before it launched on PC—its pacing is measured. It feels designed around the limitations of the consoles it's launching on, prioritising detail and depth over twitch-based combat and precise interaction. It's exactly what I'd expect from a modern Rockstar game. Also like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it, I still feel the sense of longing for what this game will look like on PC. Make no mistake: the version currently available is a preview for what GTA 6 will be at its best. It's great, but those who can wait will be treated to a superior experience.

It's also possible that the 30 fps cap will feel more restrictive once the online mode arrives—whenever that will be, and in whatever form it takes. It's one thing to handle a lower framerate within Rockstar's meticulously created campaign. It's quite another in a lobby of other players. If GTA 6's multiplayer is even half as chaotic as the current GTA Online, every frame is going to count.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/jDAfoTeqcUVNPYNfDSs8WH-1920-80.jpg
Jacob Ridley, Managing Editor, Hardware
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/2YNigoLXbckPdRPDe3stwA-1920-80.png

As I was booting up GTA 6, I was expecting to be annoyed by the game's paltry frame rate. And I was—at first. Much like Fraser, during the opening scene with Lucia, I saw my fears come to life on the big screen in front of me. Objects juddering and blurring as I swung my camera around in the cramped cell. Did I just waste £80 on GTA 6 on PS5 when I should've held my nerve for the PC version?

Truth is, the frame rate has had nowhere near as much of a negative impact on my experience while I've been traversing the Floridian wilds as Jason. In part, I think that's because there's a lot more going on, as cars, shops, people, and poultry fly past me as I break most state, federal and ethical laws. That reduces the chance of my eyes fixating on any one object and noticing the adverse effects of the game's lower fps, or the ways Rockstar has gone about covering for it.
Low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil.
Jacob Ridley

Low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil. That's not just my opinion, that's been scientifically verified (sorta) to be the opinion of PC Gamer readers . Admittedly, some motion blur may be required when the frame rate is this low, so I have played around with a few settings in GTA 6 to find the perfect balance. I'd heard through the grapevine that higher-than-default motion blur (default is 3, goes up to 10) may be preferential to reduce the more obvious juddering that is present at low fps, but whoever says that is no friend of mine. I've landed on setting motion blur to 1 on the standard PS5, as it feels the cleanest overall. I wouldn't blame anyone for turning it off entirely, especially on a more powerful console where the frame rate may not dip as much.

Of course, I do agree with the rest of this lot: in an ideal world, playing the PC version, I'd be pushing a much higher frame rate with motion blur banished to the abyss where it belongs, and a full selection of graphics settings to tinker with to my liking. Yet, to my surprise, I'm not as much of a console version curmudgeon as I thought I'd be.
Is the low frame rate noticeable? Yep. Would it be better at a higher frame rate? Also yep. Is the low frame rate a detriment to my overall enjoyment of GTA 6? Only a smidge.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/zNmjh4z2Af2rQJbH6z7TiE-1920-80.jpg
Mollie Taylor, Features Producer
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/W9VNF2qWSreZXDkwcVR2tF-1920-80.png

I don't consider myself much of a framerate snob, but I'll admit I was side-eyeing GTA 6's 30fps just a little bit. Well, that was before the game came out. Now that I have my hands on it, with roughly six hours spent lollygagging around Leonida? I'm hardly noticing it, though I'll most definitely be appreciating a smoother experience once the PC version rolls around.

Like Jacob said, motion blur definitely seems to be masking it somewhat—and I am traditionally a motion blur hater, so it's taken a little getting used to—but I'm genuinely pleasantly surprised at the balance Rockstar has managed to strike between a smooth performance and a dense, rich world.
Christopher Livingston, Senior Editor
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/wC7aUjGb8pW4neHoNS25gF-1920-80.png

GTA 6 taught me that I don't much care about frame rates as much as I expected. I got to start playing it a few weeks ago and didn't have anyone to compare notes with, and my first thought was: Huh, they got it to run at 60 fps after all! It all felt very smooth, even when I realized it was 30 fps after all. It was only a bit later I started noticing very occasional drops, like while driving during a gradual lighting chance from day to night.

That has been the big question ever since Nintendo officially revealed its console last year, and it's something that we have mused over ever since (as unlikely as it may seem at an initial glance). Their contributions were then double-confirmed by the full GTA 6 credits , which Rockstar published once launch time hit.

I’m the host of GTA 6’s “non-stop ‘80s” radio channel Vice City FM. I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I’m the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well! As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!

"I’m the host of GTA 6’s 'non-stop ‘80s' radio channel Vice City FM. I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I’m the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well!" Yankovic said. "As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!"
Somewhere out there, Weird Al is securing the love of his virtual latina wife, and I think that's beautiful.

Yankovic is just one of countless recognizable names you'll find if you scroll down the GTA 6 credits. Among the core cast, SNL alumnus Bobby Moynihan voices Cal, Jason's bumbling, conspiracy-brained buddy. The pair's criminal boss man, Brian Heder, is performed by legendary Stephen Root—who you'll likely recognize as Bill Dauterive on King of the Hill, Milton in Office Space, and all kinds of magnificent weirdos across the Coen brothers filmography.

I didn't even know he was still capable of speech.

On talk radio, you can hear Ted Lasso's Jason Sudeikis, Abbot Elementary's Janelle James, and John Leguizamo of being John Leguizamo fame. Stavros Halkias is on there doing a Conservative talk radio bit. But maybe the most compelling inclusion, for me, is that Kaleidoscope FM is hosted by Jeremy Irons. The Academy Award-winning actor. You were in Kafka, Jeremy. How'd you end up in cyber-Florida?

If I wanted to include all the recognizable names on the list, I'd need a dozen more paragraphs, so I recommend you browse the credits yourself. Or just be content in knowing that Weird Al is waiting for you. That works for me, too.

content.v: I just found a curious artifact of the Old West in GTA 6, and the best part is I stumbled across it completely by accident.
That's right, partner: Arthur Morgan's cowboy hat is in Grand Theft Auto 6, and you won't find it in some trendy Western fashion shop or in a McMansion as part of a wealthy crypto bro's collection.
If you want to wear it yourself, I'll tell you below where you can find it.
How to find Arthur Morgan's cowboy hat
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Ta3RE2kYKSQX2P9QMvvA4U-1920-80.jpg

I was out in Port Gellhorn looking for a particular kind of car for reasons completely unrelated to clothing accessories. While I was driving, I spotted a sign on the side of the road with a balloon tied to it, reading "Yard Sale" with an arrow pointing down the road.
I followed the sign which led to more yard sale signs and, yup, sure enough, the signs pointed me to an actual yard sale. And among the items for sale was a very familiar-looking hat.
It's called a "Genuine Cowboy Hat" and, this being a yard sale, it only cost $5. But I knew the second I saw it that this was no ordinary cowboy hat. Here, have a look at it from the back.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/xuWkVkcdw5ELWWUeEeVeLU-1920-80.jpg

Yep. No mistaking that. I even got a little pang of sadness thinking about good ol' Arthur Morgan. I miss him. Maybe when I'm done with GTA 6, I'll strap on my spurs and take another ride through Red Dead Redemption 2.

Directions : Head to Port Gellhorn. It's in Kelly County on the western side of the state along the coast. In the southern tip of Port Gellhorn, there's a small neighborhood of about five houses just northwest of the Dirt Merchants mod shop.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TRyze8VuFtoHQkpJMny84U-1920-80.jpg

Look for the driveway filled with yard sale clutter: furniture and electronics and such. There's a bunch of balloons, a cut-out of a nearly naked cowboy, and a big American flag flying. You'll find the hat toward the back sitting on top of a guitar case on a couch. There's also a shirt, a cap, and some shoes for sale that definitely didn't belong to Arthur.

items.title: 海盗船 Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo 评论
items.summary: Machine learning sensitivity changes to help you aim.

content.v: Corsair is continuing the 2026 trend of brands pushing out new and innovative mouse technologies . In this case, it's all in the 'PureVector' part of the name. In partnership with AimLabs, Corsair has made a mouse that can adjust sensitivity in different directions to tailor it to your movements and help you aim better.

That's the claim, anyway. In practice, I've found that PureVector hasn't improved my aim, both subjectively while gaming and objectively based on multiple AimLabs tests. Some pro players that Corsair highlights claim it's helped them, so your mileage may vary.

Apart from PureVector, though, the mouse itself deserves some attention, as it's still a very performant, lightweight mouse for competitive gaming. It has some upgrades compared to its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro , too.
Buy if…
✅ You want to try the latest tech: You might get better results than I did with PureVector. It tailors sensor sensitivity in different directions based on how you aim.
Don't buy if…
❌ You want good value for the basics: If you just want a comfy mouse with solid build quality that performs well, you can find something of better value elsewhere.
Features
Buttons
Connectivity
USB-C or 2.4 GHz wireless
Sensor
Marksman X
Switches
Optical
Feet

Max DPI
Max acceleration

Up to 8,000 Hz

Weight
Extras
Replacement skates, USB-A to USB-C cable, wireless dongle, AimLabs PureVector software integration
Price

In most ways, the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo is your standard competitive gaming mouse: lightweight, few frills, simple design, good sensor. It is lighter than most competitive mice with a solid shell, though a little heavier than its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro.

Setting aside the PureVector aiming shenanigans for a moment, probably the biggest improvement compared to the Sabre V2 Pro is its battery life, which has been doubled. Apart from that, you're getting a 42,000 DPI sensor, optical clicks, and some bigger replacement skates included in the box.
Performance
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Y3NZAqrYXRK9Zktj3VyzeB-1920-80.jpg

Now we come to the main attraction: PureVector. Corsair has designed the mouse's internals and firmware to permit different sensitivities in different directions. So, for instance, it can move slightly slower horizontally than vertically.

Corsair has worked with AimLabs to let you test your aiming in the latter software and then have the mouse adjust your directional sensitivity for you. The PureVector software within AimLabs has been made with the help of a bunch of aiming data (over 4 billion data points, apparently) and machine learning. The end result is, in theory, a mouse that can tailor its sensitivity in different directions to stop you over-shooting or under-shooting your target.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/uyAqepgt8Zb6NP6fn6L4Zm-1920-80.jpg

Again, in theory, this should also save you time when you aim, and Corsair claims it can save more time than reducing the latency of clicks—the latter is, for example, what we see the Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike and X3 Superstrike focusing on.
It's worth noting that Corsair highlights a number of pro players who say they've benefitted from this new tech. However, for my part, I haven't noticed a difference.

For reference, I play Counter-Strike 2 at about FaceIt Level 7 or Premier 18–20,000 rating (approx. top 25%). I'm far from a pro, but I'm far from the worst. In-game, I didn't notice any difference between my aim with PureVector set up and with it disabled.

I also repeatedly tested my aim in the AimLabs SpiderShot Precision test, and I actually had slightly better results using another mouse without PureVector (the SteelSeries Sensei Pro), and the latter mouse my hand was less familiar with.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/CzacNdXqfQqa9wPswJcxcm-1920-80.jpg

More than this, though, I can't help but feel that it's a bit of a band-aid solution to poor aim. If you're overshooting your shots when you aim left, for instance, you could get PureVector to lower your sensitivity in that direction. But why not instead work on training your hand not to overshoot? That way, having good aim won't be dependent on using this one mouse, and you can get used to aiming consistently in different directions.

PureVector aside, the Sabre V3 Pro performs well. The sensor is great and feels very responsive. Ditto the new optical mouse clicks. I have no complaints about its performance as a general mouse, I just don't see the use in PureVector myself. Of course, your mileage may vary, as it seems to have for some pro players.

One area where the Sabre V3 Pro does particularly shine, just like the Sabre V2 Pro, is in its light weight. This latest iteration feels even sturdier than the previous one and still manages to be lighter than most competitive gaming mice.
Battery life
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/VgQWXfEZxH7mpgU4oUwMfB-1920-80.jpg

Battery life is a definite selling point of the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector. It's a lot better than I was expecting. The Sabre V2 Pro can only manage about 70 hours at 1 kHz, and this new one doubles that to 140 hours.

I think Corsair has struck a great balance here, because it's not as light as the V2—which was 36 g—but 41 g is still incredibly light, and I'd much rather have the bigger battery than shave off those few extra grams. You're not getting any fancy wireless charging or hot-swappable batteries here, but 140 hours of battery life is great.
Ergonomics
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/zah8p3ThfSorEwDMi34feB-1920-80.jpg

The Corsair Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo is, as its excruciatingly long name suggests, pretty ergonomic. It's not the biggest ergo mouse I've used—the Zowie EC2-DW and SteelSeries Rival Pro both feel a bit bigger in-hand—but it still feels comfy under my medium-sized palm.
There's also a non-ergo, symmetrical version for the same price, and you can get carbon fiber or magnesium versions for each, if you're willing to spend even more ($200 and $230, respectively).

I like the lightweight ergonomic version, though. Its slightly smaller size, combined with its light weight, also means holding it in a fingertip or claw grip doesn't feel too bad, which isn't something you can say about many ergonomic mice. Palm grip is still the main intention here, though. Playing Counter-Strike on low sensitivity feels great.

items.title: 作为一名 PC 玩家，我在 GTA 6 中做的第一件事当然就是尝试鼠标和键盘
items.summary: We also gave steering wheels a go, too.

content.v: I am nothing if not entirely predictable. I've waited 13 years to play a new Grand Theft Auto game and the first thing I do when I finally get around to booting GTA 6 —and definitely not spoofing my home address to access it early—is jam a mouse and keyboard into my Xbox Series X just to see.

GTA 5, once it made its way to PC, was always a game I played both with a keyboard and mouse and with a controller plugged in. Keeb and rodent for shooting, especially in the first-person mode, and the controller for just getting about in the game world. It was a real best of both worlds kinda thing that the PC does so well.
It was the same with Red Dead Redemption 2, a game I completely avoided until it finally came to the PC. Keyboard and mouse for runnin' and gunnin' and a controller for horsin' around. Yeehaw.

So, I was hoping—hoping against hope, really—that I could just do the same with GTA 6. I was hoping that I could just plug in my little Mountain keyboard and my DeathAdder mouse, and it would just work.

Sadly no, there is no mouse and keyboard support for GTA 6. There is for Xbox, and my keyboard works fine just in the home screens, but as soon as you hit the game itself… nada. Keyboard and mouse support is still very much an occasional thing for Microsoft's console. It is supported, but it's on a per-game basis where devs have to actively code support into their Xbox versions of a title in order for a keyboard and mouse to work.

It's not actually that rare—some 450 games, and big games such as Cyberpunk 2077 and Alan Wake 2, have some level of support for one or both peripherals. But it is certainly not something Rockstar has spent any time putting in place when it was spending an extra year optimising the game after the delayed release. Which is a shame, given that the company has gone to great lengths to add a huge level of detail to its world to the point it almost feels like it's thought of everything.

More frustrating given that right now I bet there are Rockstar developers playing the game on keyboard and mouse in internal PC-only builds of the game. Would I have sacrificed sitting on my comfy sofa playing it writ large on my living room wall through my 4K projector just to sit at my desk with a keyboard and mouse? Maybe. It would have certainly felt like I was playing it on PC.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/LjMswP9FgPXnkPxNC7Jfr3-1920-80.jpg

Something else Rockstar hasn't put into the game is any steering wheel control. Jacob, as a racing fan, tried to get his PlayStation wheelbase running on his PS5 copy of the game… but alas that is unsupported, too. Which was a source of frustration for him as he co-opted his partner in carrying his sim rig into his living room to try it out and now she is refusing to help put it back after his failure.

But this is a situation that might have to change moving forward. The next-gen Xbox machine, codenamed Helix has already been confirmed as being able to play PC games. In a recent interview with Jason Ronald, Xbox VP of Next Gen , this was again reiterated.
"We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," says Ronald. "It is not a PC that can also play console games."

This means it's going to have to support PC games, and that potentially means baked in support for keyboard and mouse in the hardware itself, rather than enabled on a per-title basis. After all, PC games kinda take those inputs for granted, no? So, maybe Red Dead Redemption 3 on Project Helix might come with keyboard and mouse support from the get-go, even if it's not necessarily released on PC straight away.
Still, for GTA 6 right now, basically it's controller or nothing, so make sure to get yourself a good pad —that's one of the biggest upgrades I've made to my setup for GTA 6.

items.title: 现在我已经在 PS5 Pro 上玩了 GTA 6，这就是我想要的 PC 版本
items.summary: After playing GTA 6 all day yesterday on everything from the Xbox Series S up to the PS5 Pro, I'm forming a cl

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/19/gtavi-37-1795107050305.jpg
This is an opinion piece by Jackie Thomas, IGN's Senior Tech Editor who's been covering PC games and the components that make them run for more than a decade.

GTA 6 is exclusive to consoles at launch, but everyone knows a PC version will come out eventually. And when it does, it'll probably be the best way to play the game, provided you have the hardware to run it at a high frame rate.

While I know that's a tough bar to clear with prices being what they are these days, after playing GTA 6 all day yesterday on everything from the Xbox Series S up to the PS5 Pro , I'm forming a clearer picture on what a PC version of the game should look like.

Obviously, the first thing that the PC version of GTA 6 is going to be able to do that the console version can't is actually hit 60fps. Rockstar itself came out and said that a 60fps patch won't be coming to the PS5 Pro because it's simply not powerful enough. And, well, that wasn't super surprising . The PC version will be able to hit 60fps, but I think it might be a bit of a struggle for a lot of the PCs out there.

Every single current-generation console is housing an AMD Zen 2 CPU with 8 cores and 16 threads, and if we were just going off core counts alone, that would match or exceed the vast majority of gaming PCs out there, according to the Steam Hardware Survey. However, in the six years since Zen 2's debut in the Ryzen 7 2700X, IPC (Instructions per Clock) performance has risen so much that I doubt most recent 8-core CPUs are going to have the same troubles with players blowing shit up in GTA than the consoles have right now.

The problem is, unlike graphics cards , CPUs are often one of the last things people upgrade in their PCs, so I imagine there are still a lot of older 8-core CPUs out there that aren't dramatically faster than what you'd find in the PS5 and Xbox Series X. But if you do have a more recent mid-to-high end CPU like the AMD Ryzen 7000 or 9000 series or anything Intel post 12th-gen, you should be able to push GTA 6 to a higher frame rate than the consoles.

Right now, as I write this, I'm sitting next to a rig with an AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D and an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 , and if the furthest I can push this game is 60fps, I don't even know if it's going to be worth double dipping. The real difference to GTA 6's frame rate on PC probably isn't going to come from the brute force of the hardware, but the software suites. Now, Rockstar did some excellent work with the upscaling solutions available to them, and even used FSR 4.1 to great effect to get the game running as well as it did on the Xbox Series S. But, as good as FSR and PSSR are, they just aren't as good as DLSS.

My hope would be that Rockstar makes full use of Nvidia's software suite to both make for cleaner upscaling and frame generation. I know that frame gen is a controversial technology, but a game like GTA 6 is perfect for it. After all, it's a slower paced single-player open world game that doesn't need you to have lightning-fast reflexes to succeed, so the added latency won't really be a big deal.

I'll probably finish the game at 30fps on the PS5 Pro, and I'm already pretty used to that frame rate, but on PC, I'll be fully expecting to use frame gen to push that number up to 240fps on my monitor, which will make the game much smoother and easier on the eyes.

GTA 6's move to PC is going to be about more than just upping the frame rate though. As good as the game looks on console – and it looks f**king incredible – it's going to look even better on a PC that can push it to its limits. While the PS5 Pro uses ray traced global illumination, reflections and shadows, then pairs it with PSSR for a clean, beautiful image with excellent lighting, there are still some dials Rockstar can turn to bring the game to another level.

Chief among these is going to be path tracing. Back when Cyberpunk 2077 implemented its 'RT Overdrive' preset, it completely changed the way the game looked. Just looking at the PS5 Pro version of GTA 6 as a baseline, path tracing could elevate the game to a point where it's eerily close to photorealism.

Of course, implementing path tracing would have a huge hit to performance, and GTA 6 isn't exactly going to be a walk in the park for most gaming PCs. For the most part though, lighting settings would hammer your graphics card, and the biggest limiting factor for GTA 6 performance on console right now is the CPU, rather than the GPU. Again, it's hard to get metrics to see exactly how hard each processor in the PS5 Pro is being hit by GTA 6, but if the majority of the processing is being done on the CPU, adding more work for the GPU to do while it waits for the CPU probably isn't going to affect performance as much as you'd think.

Word on the street is that the PC version of GTA 6 is going to come sooner than in past generations, so we hopefully won't have to wait long to see what it can do. I personally hope Rockstar uses the PC port as an opportunity to create the ultimate version of the game. Luckily, that's exactly what it did with Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 5, even if they both had buggy launches.

items.title: 《足球经理 27》评论：恢复状态，但并非没有任性的触感
items.summary: The football management sim is back on form, but not without its wayward touches.

content.v: What is it? The latest in a long line of life-absorbing sports management sims. Release date November 10, 2026 Expect to pay $60/£50 Developer Sports Interactive Publisher Sega Reviewed on Ryzen 7 9800X3D, Radeon RX 9070XT, 16GB RAM Steam Deck TBA Link Official site

It's difficult to convey to non-players how deeply Football Manager gets under your skin. It's the kind of game that becomes your mental screensaver, the fallback topic whenever your brain isn't explicitly required to think about something else. A Slack DM came in this morning and for a second I interpreted 'DM – [Name]' as Slack assigning my colleague the defensive midfielder position. When did they add that feature? I caught myself thinking for a second.

That in itself doesn't mean Football Manager 27 is a great game. This series is capable of fostering fixation even on its off games, like last year's tile-ridden UI tangle FM26. But this new release makes meaningful progress by untangling that UI, improving the flow of the game between matches, and—the holy grail—giving you some clue as to why you're losing, and what you can do about it.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/83M7ibqz4hs4XmtkKeRdPK-1920-80.png

The latter point comes thanks to the introduction of the 'tactical effectiveness' system. This is a visual rating of all the factors that affect your team's performance, and it lives in your tactics screen as a colour-coded scale. The better all those underlying factors are working, the higher your tactical effectiveness scale goes. Click on it and you see under the hood of FM's simulation, at all the elements which determine your squad's performance, from individual player ability and training effectiveness to each player's degree of buy-in to your tactical vision.

That screen gives a degree of transparency to what's deciding whether you win or lose, and having played these games since Championship Manager 2, I've been wishing for that transparency for a long time.

But it's not without its issues. This being the introduction of this new system, its effects feel overly exaggerated. If your team has a low tactical effectiveness they'll lollop about on the pitch like it's their first day on Earth, even in the most basic formations that my school's under 11s side could execute. It's extremely frustrating to watch the sport's absolute elite wandering about in the final third like they've forgotten where the goal is, or witness Champions League-calibre centre backs totally baffled by their markers running in a straight line towards goal. This is probably how it feels to be a Man United manager in real life, but it still feels like a failing of the match engine to visualise poor tactical effectiveness in a true-to-life way.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/48SAvSZS3MABAydj4kXRPK-1920-80.png

The flipside of that coin is that there's a lot of gratification to be had in increasing that TE scale, and FM 27 does a good job of surfacing the ways to do it. It means setting more tactical familiarity sessions in the training screen, a doorway I haven't personally darkened for years as a manager since it allowed me to delegate that task to my assistant. It also finds its way into recruitment, showing you a rough prediction of how well a player will contribute to that all-important rating even before you sign them. I really enjoy this new way of thinking about signings, and relish the chance to be proactive about improving performances instead of changing things at random and crossing my fingers.

On the pitch, there's some modest progress since last year. New animations, specifically flair passes and players recovering from a stumble after being shoulder-barged, tell you something useful about that player's attributes and how they can be used. Meanwhile on the presentation front, there are a few new angles during pre-match sequences and trophy ceremonies.

There's also a lot of the usual release-era nonsense. In my save I seem to have a goal waved off for offside every twenty minutes, and keepers seem to have started coating their boots and gloves in teflon when receiving the most straightforward backpasses or clearing up routine balls. These odd glitches happen every year before the first few patches roll out, and update 27.1.0 does seem to address most of the odd match engine behaviour I've noticed.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/CpL2QjBHbR8tHNMRS3SShJ-1920-80.png

But I'm disappointed that progress is that gradual. Particularly as FM's move to the Unity engine was so disruptive, prompting the series to skip a year. I expected that engine switch might mean the match engine evolves more quickly, but that doesn't seem to be the case based on this release.

Instead, the really significant additions and improvements can be found in the nooks and crannies, the boring bits you wouldn't write about in the Steam description. How do you make navigable menus, more game setup customization options and quicker progress between matches sound sexy? Nevertheless, these are the changes that add up and make FM 27 feel much more enjoyable than last year's game.

The prime example of these small but mighty changes is the 'continue flow'. When you start a new game, you can now control how often the game stops the passage of time to return you to your inbox after you hit 'continue'. Hardly the most exciting feature on paper, but it addresses a crucial and longstanding problem: progress had become punitively slow. More than any loss at home to a relegation side or any unreasonable telling-off from the board, it was this feeling of wading nose-deep through molasses that sapped my desire to keep playing recent FM games, and it turns out that fixing the problem is as simple as selecting the 'streamlined' continue flow so that the game stops progressing time less often and moves you from match to match at a faster rate.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/74JdTBdvLmhRPrqnWyQ9QK-1920-80.png

This is a game about setting long-term plans and watching them come to fruition. Winning one match isn't where the payoff comes, it's three seasons in when you see how much your youth academy graduate's stats have developed. So it really does matter that FM 27 hastens the pace and you can see those long term plans resolve.

There's been something of a deft Cruyff turn from Sports Interactive on the direction of its UI this year, after the overhaul in FM 26 was received as positively as a taxation on laughter. The menu tiles have been pared right back, menus themselves are much faster to load and in general it's more intuitive to get to the screens you're looking for.

That doesn't mean Football Manager 27 has a good UI. I still too often find myself hunting for basic actions now buried several menus deep, like having to click Portal - Career - My Profile - Actions - Go On Holiday to start simming through fixtures. For reference, here's how it worked in Championship Manager 01/02: [Manager Name] - Go On Holiday.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/m6Fvji2VLaoQU7pe79coNJ-1920-80.png

I still find myself struggling to process the morass of information being thrown at me by certain menus too, particularly the matchday screens. More detail does not equal more fun, and most of these info panels are useless to me, serving only to obscure the bits I do want to check. There's more customisation this year to allow what these menus show you, but you can't remove info panels entirely or simplify screens.

items.title: “我只关心抢劫”：43 名士兵重新入伍，享受 4 天周末玩 GTA 6
items.summary: That's one way to get a long weekend.

content.v: We got confirmation a couple of months ago that the US Army's 3rd Infantry Division was offering a four-day pass to play Grand Theft Auto 6 for soldiers who re-enlist for at least two years. And now the time has come to collect.

Talking to Task & Purpose one soldier who took advantage of the program, Sgt. Jamire Smith, described how he's planning to spend the long weekend: "I'm all campaign. I’m all about the heist. I think I have a good 24 hours to waste on it.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vxtVvoa7uzxJRPg8BgtrXQ-1920-80.jpg

"I was actually in the process of getting out, I was towards my final stages of getting out … but my company and the battalion helped me navigate through that and they showed me that there’s still a need for me, and that I am still a clear and value asset to the team, and so that’s really what drove me to say 'let’s keep going, let’s keep driving'. Maybe be a lifer in this, since I already made it my career."
In total 43 soldiers re-enlisted through the GTA 6 incentive, an idea that was born from Staff Sgt. Brittany Wolfer.

"It's not supposed to be the deciding factor," Wolfer says. "There is always going to be a disconnect between your senior command and your lowest soldier. So how do you bridge that gap to where that lower soldier still knows that their battalion commander or their senior leadership cares about them and sees what they're interested in. And that’s kind of what this was for."

Wolfer first brought the idea to her battalion commander who actually played GTA 2 back in the day and so was up for trying the incentive out. "I came into [the unit], there hadn’t been a counsellor for about eight months, so there was a lot of gaps and things that were falling through because the soldiers didn’t have that presence within the formation," Wolfer adds. "This kind of was just a way to grab people's attention and kind of be like, 'Hey, here I am. I’m the person you’re gonna come talk to,' and [it] kind of snowballed from there."

items.title: GTA 6 的迪士尼世界戏仿在哪里？ Rockstar North 联合工作室负责人解释未到场的情况
items.summary: GTA 6 lacks a parody of Disney World partially because developer Rockstar felt there wasn't a strong enough na

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/19/gtavi-16-1795106399624.jpg

GTA 6 lacks a parody of Disney World partially because developer Rockstar felt there wasn't a strong enough narrative justification for all the work that would have to go into meeting player expectations.

In an interview with VGC , Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson was asked why GTA 6 doesn't feature a Disney World parody . He noted that the team didn't think it supported the game's narrative and tone enough to make it worth the time and effort.

“The obvious reason?” Nelson said with a laugh, “It’s about whether there’s a narrative reason to spend that time to make a fully functioning theme park. We just figure out what we do need to support the story and support the feeling of being in Leonida. A theme park would represent a lot of work that we didn’t have, and we didn’t have a strong narrative reason to send them there."

This sense that Rockstar had a blank check for GTA 6's development is something Nelson has pushed back on multiple times in the run up to the game's launch. Nelson recently touched on this issue in an interview with IGN , where he conceded that Rockstar's development approach did have to be managed, because without any guardrails, “every team will go crazy and go on forever.”

“And so there’s a bit of a contract there between all of us, including ourselves; having checks and balances in terms of where we push, how far we push, how hard we push, and how much resource [something] is worth, because everything is time and resource spent,” he said. “And contrary to what people think, we don’t have infinite money or time, or resource. So we do have to make decisions.”

VGC asked whether the decision to steer clear of Disney World was rooted in having to decide how many rides there would be, how fun they actually are, and making it all worthwhile. "Yeah, that’s the challenge: where do you stop?" said Nelson. "When do you feel like it’s enough? We went as hard as we could on interiors, but you’ve got to fill them – they have to feel natural.”

GTA 5 allowed players to visit a pier which had a ferris wheel and a rollercoaster, and these rides were pretty boring. It was something to do one time and then never think about ever again. If you're going to a parody of Disney World, it would need to feel massive and alive so that it lives up to the hype.

Rockstar has been pretty forthcoming about its decisions to not include certain things, in spite of the game being massive and freeing. GTA 6 doesn't allow you to pick up prostitutes , for example. This is a staple of the franchise and this decision has rubbed some people the wrong way. Rockstar, however, believes it is counter-intuitive to the story it is trying to tell about two protagonists who are madly in love.

content.v: Grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty of famous faces and voices behind its many, many characters. From Bobby Moynihan as your verbose bestie to Weird Al Yankovic as a radio host, there's plenty of star power here--and you can even spot an influential figure from GTA history making a quick cameo.
Spoilers below
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/GTA-6-Cameo_b53f6a.jpg?w=636

In one of the later missions, players accompany Boobie on one of his errands. Once they reach a new club, Boobie meets up with Big Mike and throws a few jibes at the local help sweeping the floor. That "little Santa" with the broom? None other than Rockstar Games president Sam Houser, who doesn't speak a single word in his brief appearance. As an added touch, Houser's digital doppelganger wears a white t-shirt with the Rockstar Games logo.
Because the thumbnail for it is a big ol' spoiler, you can click this link to see the Houser cameo for yourself.

This isn't the first time that Houser has cameoed in one of his studio's games. In GTA 3, he voiced one of the Ammu-Nation store clerks, and in GTA: San Andreas, a statue of that Ammu-Nation employee could be found in the game's Downtown Square area. Beyond minor background pedestrian and gangster voice roles in San Andreas and GTA 4, Houser has generally kept a low profile, focusing instead on developing the studio's games .

With GTA 6 launching to major critical and commercial success, Houser has also issued a rare statement to mark the occasion. "This is a narrative set in a world of possibilities--and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels and concludes," he said. Meanwhile, Houser's brother, Dan Houser, is working on an open-world comedy game at Absurd Ventures, the studio he founded after leaving Rockstar Games in 2020.

content.v: It's Grand Theft Auto VI day around the world--the game is really good , as it turns out. While players are out exploring the massive in-game map or checking their in-game phones as much as they check their real-life ones, Rockstar has celebrated the occasion by releasing the full cast list for its new crime epic.

Nestled among celebrity names like Bad Bunny, "Weird Al" Yankovic, Brigitte Nielsen, Stephen Root, and Bobby Moynihan is a name that will surprise many longtime Rockstar fans. It's also, potentially, a GTA VI spoiler, so we're going to put it below a selfie of co-protagonist Jason Duval.
Seriously, if you want to go into Grand Theft Auto VI spoiler-free, look away now .
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/1a1f3560f7889-screenshotUrl.jpg?w=636
Alright, if you're still here, then you're in for the spoiler. Ready? Here goes:

One of the names listed on the credits is Michael Hollick, playing a role known only as "The Hitman." If that's setting off a signal to established Grand Theft Auto fans, it's because Michael Hollick is also the voice of GTA IV protagonist--and occasional hitman--Niko Bellic.

Hollick's involvement in GTA VI is surprising, considering how just after GTA IV's release in 2008, he publicly criticized Rockstar for his payment on the project. As reported by CNET by way of the New York Times, Hollick reportedly was paid $100,000 for 15 months of work on the project.
Whether or not this is actually a spoiler remains to be seen, but with Grand Theft Auto VI now available on both PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, we imagine the truth will be revealed soon enough.

items.title: 一款新的《辐射》游戏在澳大利亚获得评级，这是一款隐藏物品游戏
items.summary: It's called A Wasteland Full of Cats, and I think it sounds great.

content.v: I'm not quite sure what to make of this so I'm going to just put it out there: A new Fallout game might soon be headed our way, and it's a hidden object game.
A Wasteland Full of Cats, as it's known, recently appeared on the Australian Classification Board website (via the Fallout subreddit ), and the title pretty much says it all. From the rating:

This game is a hidden object game and the objects you need to find are cats. You play as one of the cats in the Vault. One day there is an accident in the Vault and all of the cats who live there escape out into the Wasteland. It is up to you with the help of some NPCs you meet along the way to find them and return them to the Vault. This game has 14 locations, 33 rooms + a vault of recognizable levels from the Fallout franchise with light puzzle mechanics that uncover some hidden levels that aren’t required to finish the game. There is a final boss fight where the player has to shoot some Rad roaches in order to save the last remaining cats and humans.

The rating says A Wasteland Full of Cats is being made by Devcats, the Brazilian studio behind the Full of Cats game series, and—this is the really interesting part—it's being made "in partnership with Bethesda and the Fallout franchise."

Is this legit? Is the next Fallout release a hidden object game? I don't know, but I do know that the Australian Classification Board generally isn't party to pranks and hoaxes. I also know that a lot of Fallout fans will be rolling their eyes and moaning at the idea of hidden object Fallout, but hear me out: Hidden object games are good, actually .

Sure, you're not going to be prowling through horrific underground labs or gunning down super mutants in a life-or-death struggle for survival. But hidden object games are chill and relaxing, a great way to wind down after a busy day robbing liquor stores and shooting cops with your significant other. They're a simpler kind of fun, which makes them kind of kin to the really early days of videogames, when we were all ready to accept that a blocky blob of pink on the screen was a dragon.

All of which is to say that even if you have no interest in playing a Fallout hidden object game (although I think you should), it's far from unthinkable that Bethesda would make one—or have someone make one for it, I suppose. (I would also point out that you could say basically the same thing about Fallout Shelter , and it's been chugging happily along for well over a decade now.)

I've reached out to Bethesda and Devcats about A Wasteland Full of Cats, and will update if I receive a reply. I've also captured a screen of the Australian Classification Board rating, just in case they take it down.

items.title: GTA 6：您不想错过的可选任务
items.summary: GTA 6 is full of optional activities, but some are more essential than others. These are the seven side missio

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/19/optional-blog-c-1795092990860.jpg

This article is designed to point you in the direction of some of GTA 6’s best side missions. While there are no story spoilers , I will be guiding you on how to find each quest-giver to make sure you don’t miss them!

Jason and Lucia’s story in GTA 6 is so compelling that you’ll be easily tempted into mainlining their epic tale. But outside of those main missions are some of Leonida’s most weird and wonderful encounters, with multi-stage storylines that you’ll rarely be able to guess where they end up. Trust me, you don’t want to risk skipping the game’s best side activities.

Don’t worry, I won’t be revealing how these quests develop. Instead, I’ll just be showing you where to start them, or in the instances where these missions will come directly to you, why you won’t want to pass on something that looks underwhelming on the surface. Anyway, let’s get on with it. Here are the seven optional missions in GTA 6 you won’t want to miss.
Skunk Ape
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/19/optional-blog-a-1795089410749.jpg

Find yourself peacefully sailing through the Grassrivers, only for that peace to be broken by an ungodly screaming, howling, sort of noise? Well, track down the source, and you’ll find one of the first truly odd things you can witness in GTA 6. Following the stench wafting from a deer carcass into the overgrowth will guide you to a totem that wouldn’t look too out of place in the first series of True Detective. You won’t be looking at it for long, though, before passing out; a pair of legs is the last thing you see.

This could be the end of this particular tale, unless you’re a keen reader of posters, that is. Dotted around the starting area of Key Lento are various flyers asking for information on “Skunk Ape”. Once read, a new contact will be added to your phone. Call Kirk, and he’ll offer to meet up at night, where you can carry on delving into the mystery. Don’t worry, he’s very friendly, and nothing sinister will occur from this point forward.
Kyle
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/19/gta-6-kyle-1795091108063.jpg

At the beginning of chapter two, you’ll be pointed in the direction of Kyle McKittrick, a local farmer in the Frogswater area who is in need of a pilot. Turns out, he’s recently broken his arm, so he needs help dusting his crops. That’s where you come in. Take off into the skies and follow his car around, making sure to feed his plants with all of the sweet nutrients they need. On the surface, this may sound like a rather mundane affair, and, to be fair, your first encounter with him will be. But revisit him whenever he’s in need of assistance and the true nature of the questline reveals itself. You’ll never look at a strawberry in the same way again.

The Official GTA 6 Guide, Only on IGN Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .
No Flushers
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/19/optional-blog-b-1795089394389.jpg

Listen to any of the radio station news reports early in the game and you may well hear stories about a “No Flushers” movement — a group proposing a conspiracy theory related to Leonida’s waste management. Actually meeting the people involved won’t come naturally, though. In fact, it wasn’t until hour 80 of my playthrough that I stopped at a notice board in Port Gellhorn to scan a bulletin that led me to them. Once contacted, you’ll be asked to go to a waffle restaurant in Vice City where you’ll meet Dr. Merle. A man with a plan, he’ll flush on this one occasion after eating an intentionally stomach-churning selection from the menu, thus starting the quest for the truth. Follow the tracker he quite literally dumped into the sewage pipes and find where it leads for yourself. It’s bonkers.
Dodo Rising
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/19/optional-blog-c-1795089378743.jpg

There are many different ways to find some of Leonida’s most interesting side missions. Some spin-off from characters you’ll meet in the main story, others are found by the roadside, and some can even be triggered by a quick browse of Snapmatic. That’s how I stumbled upon Dodo Rising, an animal rights group protesting a chimp sanctuary near Vice City International Airport. Talk to them, hand over your info, and you’ll be roped into their fight as you infiltrate their target in an effort to save the apes. And that’s just the first of many missions you’ll be taking on with various quirky members of Dodo Rising, culminating in one of GTA 6’s most bizarre moments.
Yago
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/19/gta-6-yago-1795091124569.jpg

Not all of these missions are weird, though. Some are much more grounded and can surprise in more traditional ways. That’s the case with Yago, a hopeful street racer you first meet during chapter three. What on the surface looks like a pretty straightforward set of Tokyo Drift-esque races later reveals itself to be much more of a human story with a memorable ending. Even if racing isn’t your favourite GTA 6 side activity, it's very much worth playing through them just to see the hidden depths of Yago’s story, as his inner turmoil battles against the situation he finds himself in.
Papa Audacity
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/19/gta-6-papa-audacity-1795091138786.jpg

Who doesn’t love to see a crypto scheme crumble? Well, in GTA 6, maybe it could actually be of benefit to jump on the Bitcoin train if money is foremost on your mind. Such an opportunity presents itself near Ocean Beach in Vice City, with the stuntman extraordinaire, Papa Audacity. This showman/charlatan, depending on your viewpoint, ropes Jason and Lucia into several marketing campaigns for the launch of his Audacity coin. It not only involves several very funny interactions with him and his cronies across the city, but also introduces you to the many different types of stunt challenges that are available to you in its open world. Your first meeting with him may not go quite to plan, but fear not, the type of evil that lurks in the blockchain always finds a way of returning.
Cellerica
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/19/gta-6-cellerica-1795091152982.jpg

And finally, Lucia’s friend Andy plays a big part in chapter one of GTA 6, but she returns much later on as an optional mission giver. Having moved from her Key Lento surroundings, she’s got a new home and job in the plush suburb of Belville, and invites Lucia to visit her. Little does Lucia know that this is to be something more than a friendly house call. Instead, she’s roped into helping out with some deliveries for Cellerica, an unusual new business program.

Deliver your first package to the women around town, and from there you can continue to climb up that Cellerica chain. It’s worth doing to see the story play out, even if it soon seems like a really bad idea to do so. I don’t know about you, but I’d rather set myself on fire than join what I’m sure is a perfectly legitimate business with nothing to hide.

And these are just a handful. There are many, many more mysteries and side quests to find around Leonida. Some are even weirder and wilder than any listed above. Like, for example, if you happen to see an abandoned car near the Starlet Motel with a trail of clothes stretching into the woods, go and check that one out for yourself. If you’re brave enough.
